recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If OO later wants to broaden the comment for additional unknown-subject scenarios, that should be handled as a separate work-group decision rather than as FHIR-5704 reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-5704 asked why Observation.subject was 0..1 instead of 1..1 given that observations have no value without a subject; the Published / Not Persuasive with Modification resolution kept 0..1 because devices may emit observations without knowing the subject and requested a comment explaining that case.
initial_application: Commit c44da32291a8d69db09d2f1103b5d172fae2ee6f applied the issue by adding the [#5704] marker and wording that one would expect 1..1 but that the subject may be missing when a device does not know the patient. Later source rework preserved that decision in source/observation/structuredefinition-Observation.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes Observation, so the Observation StructureDefinition is current build-scope source. The current element has committee note [#5704], min 0, max 1, and the device-missing-subject comment. Nearby historical issues FHIR-3447 and FHIR-7156 concern the same element's definition/comment history but do not supersede the FHIR-5704 cardinality decision. Community searches found no later final core decision requiring Observation.subject to become 1..1.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because no source change is needed: the current build-scope source already implements the FHIR-5704 decision.
